This wave is characterized by its ability to stimulate rather than inhibit, leading to widespread bodily activity. The diffusion of these effects implies that individual sensations propagate throughout the body according to physical laws—specifically, diffusion equations—which govern how signals spread through tissues. The vascular response demonstrates that such stimulation directly affects circulation independent of cardiac function, indicating a direct neuromuscular link. These primitives form a closed-loop system: sensory input → neural discharge → systemic diffusion → vascular reaction. Failure occurs when neural pathways are interrupted, halting both wave propagation and downstream effects. The mathematical structure supports a continuous-time Markov process for modeling autonomic transitions.
